get.description:
One document, through access.can(read).

Scope: a tenant token's workspace wins over ``X-Markdrop-Workspace`` (set by
the edge on a workspace's own domain; unsigned, so it can only narrow).

Renamed documents (Q4): a slug that is in some document's ``old_slugs``
answers — only to a caller who can read that document — ``200
{"moved": true, "slug": <current>, "url", "workspace_url", "folder_path"}``
with header ``X-Markdrop-Moved: <current>``; the page then 307s to the
canonical address. Anyone else gets exactly the denial the current slug
would give them (404 / 401 + gate), never the new slug.

post.description:
A9: the owner replaces a leaked edit secret. The old one stops working
at once; the new one is returned once.
Attach an anonymous document to the logged-in account (proven via secret).

Import a copy of a readable document into the caller's account.

Owned by the caller with a fresh slug, no password and no expiry; born
private unless the source is plainly public (Q3). 404/401/403 exactly as a
read of the source would answer.

patch.description:
A document's password and expiry, without its content (the share
dialog's "More options"). can(edit_settings): the owner or the edit
secret. Same transition as ``PUT /{slug}`` with those fields: a new
password narrows (epoch bump, bytes closed first, cache purge awaited);
removing it widens; an expiry books its purge. A past date is 422.

post.description:
Flag a document for abuse (public, rate-limited). Always 202; stored
only when the slug exists.

get.description: Feature gate + quota for the UI. Safe to call when nothing is configured.

post.description: Verify the uploaded blob, then publish it at a slug.

Publish pasted HTML directly — the most-requested flow.

Small enough that a presigned round trip would be pointless; anything larger
should go through the file-upload path.

patch.description:
Edit an artifact's title (owner, editors, members on non-private files)
or its password / expiry (owner only, A3).

Separate from the markdown update route because that one requires a
`content` body, which an artifact doesn't have. Publicity, the access epoch,
cache purges and live events follow from services/transitions.py.

put.description:
Swap the file behind an artifact, keeping its URL and settings.

Single file → single file: can(replace_file) — the owner, editor grantees
and workspace members on non-private files (Q6); counted against the
**owner's** quota, and a non-owner whose upload would need the owner's old
versions dropped gets 507 instead. Either side a zipped site:
can(replace_bundle) — owner only.

Same verify-then-commit shape as creation: the object is HEADed for its real
size and type before anything is written, and the previous object (or bundle
prefix) is freed only once the swap has succeeded.

post.description:
200 with the result, or 202 ``{state: "verifying", upload_id}`` when the
sha256 check outlasts the wait: poll ``GET /uploads/{id}`` until ``state``
is "done" (``result``) or "failed" (``error``). Calling it again on a
finished upload returns the same result.

get.description:
Render an ASCII/box-drawing diagram to PNG.

Public and unauthenticated by design: Google's markdown→Doc converter fetches
this URL anonymously while importing an exported document. The diagram text is
carried (compressed) in ``d`` — nothing is read from the database.

Render a Mermaid diagram to PNG (public — Google's converter fetches it).

Delegates to Kroki server-side; on any failure we fall back to rendering the
Mermaid source as a monospace image so the export never silently loses it.
Render a LaTeX expression to PNG (public — Google's converter fetches it).

Return the Google consent URL. The frontend redirects the browser to it.

The logged-in user id is signed into the OAuth ``state`` so the callback can
attribute the returned refresh token without an Authorization header.
Handle Google's redirect: store the encrypted refresh token on the user.

post.description:
Revoke the grant at Google, then forget the stored token.

We revoke on Google's side first so the user is fully disconnected (the app
loses all Drive access), then clear locally regardless of whether the revoke
call succeeded — a dead/network-failed token must not leave the account stuck
in a "connected" state.

Create the linked Google Doc, or refresh it from the current content.

First call creates a Doc (Phase 1). Subsequent calls update the same Doc
in place (Phase 2). Markdown stays the source of truth.

patch.description: Set the display name (used for passwordless email accounts with no name).

get.description: Redirect the browser to Google's consent screen.
Handle Google's redirect: exchange code, upsert user, issue our session.

post.description: Email the caller a login code + magic link. Always returns {status: sent}.
Verify a 6-digit OTP and return a session token (used by the frontend form).

get.description: Consume a magic link and redirect to the frontend with a session token.

One-click opt-out of bulk email. Public by design.

Mail clients hit this unauthenticated via List-Unsubscribe, so authority
comes from the signed token (HMAC(AUTH_SECRET, "unsub:{uid}")) rather than a
session. It only ever stops mail, so there is nothing to escalate even if a
link leaks. Transactional mail (sign-in codes, invitations) is unaffected:
those are never bulk sends.

Also served at /api/v1/unsubscribe (``unsubscribe_alias_router`` below):
campaigns sent before the URL fix link there.

post.description: RFC 8058 one-click: some clients POST rather than GET.

get.description:
Aggregated analytics: can(view_stats) — the owner only. A reader who
isn't the owner gets 403, anyone else the read denial (404).

Up to 50 people to suggest in the share dialog.

Only two sources, both people the caller already has a relationship with:
addresses they have granted document access to themselves, and members of
workspaces they belong to (whom any member can already list). It is never a
search over all users -- that would turn the share box into an oracle for
"does this address have an account here". For the same reason a grant-only
contact carries no name: the share list never showed one either.

`q` narrows by case-insensitive substring of email or name. Most recently
shared-with first, then co-members by name. The caller is never included.

post.description: Create a personal API token (raw value returned once).

get.description:
A frame of the owner's video at ``t`` seconds (rounded), as a JPEG.
404 when it isn't a video, or frames can't be made here.

The "Turn off weekly emails" link. It asks before acting: mail scanners
open every link in an email, and a GET that acted would turn the email off
for people who never clicked. The button (and one-click) POSTs.

post.description: The page's button, and RFC 8058 one-click from List-Unsubscribe-Post.

Create + link a document from the editor (owned by the caller).

A markdown file becomes a markdown document; an .html (or other text
artifact) file becomes an artifact, so it publishes as a rendered page
rather than as escaped source. Both sync through the same endpoints below,
so the editor needs no second protocol.

get.description: Full pull of the current server content.

put.description: Push local content. 409 (with current content) if base_rev is stale.

get.description: Cheap revision check for polling.

post.description: Record a bug report or feature request. Always returns {status: received}.

delete.description:
Delete a workspace and everything that belongs to it.

Shared documents are released, not deleted -- they belong to their owners,
not to the workspace.

post.description:
Invite someone by email.

Rate-limited by the hour rather than the minute, because the thing being
spent here is not our CPU — it is someone else's inbox, and this endpoint
will happily send mail to an address its caller does not own.

Upload a favicon or logo.

The stored URL is returned but not saved onto the workspace here: the
settings form owns that, and saving a field the user hasn't confirmed would
make "upload, change your mind, close the tab" leave the wrong logo live.

Attach a verified host so the edge will terminate TLS for it.

Returns 501 rather than a 500 when no hosting credentials are configured:
that is a deployment that hasn't enabled the integration, not a fault, and
the caller should be told to finish the step by hand.
Take a verified domain off the air without discarding its verification.

get.description:
Which DNS panel this customer is about to open.

A separate endpoint rather than a field on the domain list, because it costs
a live DNS lookup and the list is rendered on every visit to the tab. The UI
asks for it only while the setup instructions are actually on screen, and
only admins see those.

put.description:
Choose the domain this workspace is addressed by.

Admin, because it changes the address printed on every preview card and
handed out by the library — the workspace's public face, not one person's
preference.

patch.description:
Rename and/or move (``parent_id`` present; null = top level). Admin+
(A10). The subtree's depth is validated, every document below gets its new
path, and all of them are purged.

get.description:
"Preview as": what ``as`` would see in this folder, and what is hidden
from them and why — among the items the caller can see (services/preview.py).
Member+; ``as=email`` admin+ (it reveals that person's grants).

post.description:
Batch refile (drag-and-drop): member+ for documents they can read. All
are checked before any moves; one refusal refuses the batch.

The owner files their own documents (D1); level unchanged unless
``access`` is given.

Unshare (D2/D4): the owner always (even after leaving), or an admin —
including redacted rows, by ``handles`` (``id_token`` from /items).
``workspace`` level becomes ``private``; a link document leaving a sign-in
workspace becomes private (Q2). Returns ``{items:[{slug, access_after}]}``
(``slug`` is null for a handle the caller can't read).

put.description:
D2: a folder link shows each visitor only what they could already open.
It never changes any document's access. ``hidden`` lists the items the
caller can read that the link's audience couldn't.

get.description: The folder's share (same shape as the PUT), or 404 when not shared.

post.description:
M5: owner → any existing member — viewers included: it is the owner's
explicit choice, and the new owner can change their own standing. The old
owner becomes admin. Docs, grants and domains are unchanged.

get.description:
A shared folder: ``{workspace:{name, branding…}, folder:{name, path,
breadcrumbs:[{name, path}]}, subfolders:[{name, path, count}], items:[{slug,
title, kind, mime, url, size_bytes?, updated_at, poster_url?}]}`` — paths
relative to the shared root; items filtered to what this caller can read.
Level ``workspace`` needs a member (else 401 signin / 404).

What this link is for — shown before anyone commits to anything.

Resolved invitations still return 200 rather than an error, because "this was
already accepted" and "you were uninvited" are answers the reader needs, and
a 4xx here would leave the page with nothing to say.

delete.description: Unshare, not delete. The document goes back to its owner untouched.

post.description:
Batch level change ("Open up the K you own"): owner-only per document,
each through the same rules as PUT /{slug}/access/level. Per-slug results
``{results:[{slug, ok, error?}]}``.

get.description:
The sharing state, for anyone holding a role on the document (A6).

A reader who merely has the link (no role) gets 404: the owner's address
and the grantee list are not something a link exposes. Viewers see their
own role and the owner's display name; the grantee list (and the owner's
address) is for the owner and editors.

post.description:
Share with a named person, optionally telling them.

A failed notification does **not** undo the grant: the access is real and
correct, the email is a courtesy. The response says whether it went.

ArtifactCreateRequest.title: ArtifactCreateRequest
ArtifactCreateRequest.description: Step 2: confirm an uploaded blob and mint the shareable document.

ArtifactPasteRequest.title: ArtifactPasteRequest
ArtifactPasteRequest.description: Paste-an-HTML-page shortcut — no presigned round trip for small pages.

ArtifactReplaceRequest.title: ArtifactReplaceRequest
ArtifactReplaceRequest.description: Swap the underlying file while keeping the slug, password and expiry.

ArtifactSettingsRequest.title: ArtifactSettingsRequest
ArtifactSettingsRequest.description:
Owner-editable settings. Every field is optional — omitted means unchanged.

Separate from ``DocumentUpdate`` because that schema requires ``content``,
which an artifact doesn't have (its bytes live in R2).

ArtifactStatusResponse.title: ArtifactStatusResponse
ArtifactStatusResponse.description: Drives UI gating — the feature stays hidden until R2 is wired up.

ArtifactUploadUrlRequest.title: ArtifactUploadUrlRequest
ArtifactUploadUrlRequest.description: Step 1 of the upload: ask for a presigned PUT.

BrandingPayload.title: BrandingPayload
BrandingPayload.description: Every field optional — an unset workspace looks exactly like Markdrop.

ContactItem.title: ContactItem
ContactItem.description:
Someone the signed-in user may be offered as a share suggestion.

Only ever drawn from people the user already has a relationship with — see
`routers.me.list_contacts`. Never a global user search.

DnsProviderHint.title: DnsProviderHint
DnsProviderHint.description:
Who runs this domain's DNS, so the instructions can use their words.

Everything is optional: an unrecognised provider falls back to the generic
instructions, which is what every customer sees today.

DocumentSettingsRequest.title: DocumentSettingsRequest
DocumentSettingsRequest.description:
``PATCH /documents/{slug}/settings``: a document's password and expiry
without resending its content (the share dialog's "More options"). Every
field is optional; omitted means unchanged. ``read_password: ""`` removes
the password, like ``remove_password: true``.

InvitePreview.title: InvitePreview
InvitePreview.description:
What the person holding the link is shown before deciding.

Names the workspace, the inviter and the address it was sent to, and nothing
else — in particular not who else is a member. The recipient already knows
their own address; everything here was in the email they were sent.

InviteResponse.title: InviteResponse
InviteResponse.description:
The admin-facing view of an invitation. Deliberately has no token field:
the raw token exists for exactly as long as it takes to compose the email,
and putting it in an API response would turn any workspace admin into a
credential oracle for an address they do not control.

WorkspaceDeleteRequest.title: WorkspaceDeleteRequest
WorkspaceDeleteRequest.description: The workspace's own name, typed back. See `services.workspace.delete_workspace`.
